Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: New SCP idea Scylla and Charybdis

alright here's why

Scp 5083 - The Reality Remote

The title already made me do -1. It's formatted wrong. SCP is suppose to be uppercase and The Reality Remote part shouldn't be there.

Item #: SCP-5083

Uhhh only the parts before the : gets bolded. This applies to every single one.

SCP-5083 is to be kept in a wooden box measuring 5.5 inches in width and 3.5 inches in length.

This is a common problem with newer SCP writers, they put everything in boxes. You can just say SCP-XXXX is put in a locker. Not everything needs it's own room. Also the site uses meters not inches.

Due to SCP-5083 being used for personal gain becoming a possibility, SCP-5083's box is to be under 24/7 surveillance.

Reading on the effects of the SCP, I don't really understand this. If it was a box that gave you 1 million dollars but also blew up a small town then yeah sure but all this SCP does is change reality. Also I'm pretty sure everything is under constant surveillance.

Any individual attempting to interact in any way with SCP-5083 without authorization from the 05-Council is to be immediately terminated.

Uh, what. I'm like 95% sure that termination would be kind of strict. Unless this can cause an end of the world scenario then probably not have the termination. Also it's O5 not 05.

SCP-5083 is a standard black universal tv remote measuring 2 inches in width and 7.5 inches in length.

You don't have to say every since detail unless it's anomalous. For example: I don't have to say "SCP-XXXX is a computer that has a screen the size of 0.4318 meters." Like that's kind of silly. It would be acceptable if it was something like "SCP-XXXX is an Asian Child measuring 492 feet in height".

Each button on SCP-5038 seemingly has a different effect on reality but can be made to effect one specific item or individual by pointing SCP-5083 at the target and pressing a button.

And that's the end… It would have really been spiced up with some test logs. I wanna see what scientists can do with this remote. Like what can you do with it

Overall, go to the forums. This is probably a cold post.

item.title: Re: Cat that talks in the voice of deceased relatives SCP Greenlight Request
item.content:encoded:
The primary idea is that the Cat is a way for people to better cope with the trauma of losing a loved one and as such is helpful. The actual things that the cat says are not able to be recorded, with them instead appearing as normal feline vocalizations, and so it leaves the reader to fill in the blanks of the specific emotional advice that is being given, which can thus allow the reader to project more of their own feelings onto the cat. There is also the idea that the cat is somewhat mysterious as its origin is unclear and it has physical properties abnormal of cats. There is also the possibility that the cat could affect other SCPs which could lead to interesting scenarios of writing about how the cat interacts with other SCPs.

item.title: My joke scp idea. SCP-5127-J
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5127-J is a translucent ghost version of Michael Gary Scott, the branch manager of Dunder Mifflin Scranton SCP-5127-J first appeared when Steve Carell finished The Office in 2011. Before the foundation knew anything about SCP-5127-J, It was roaming Steve Carell's mansion. After Steve Carrel said anything, SCP-5127-J responded with "That's what she said" which made anything Steve said seem wrong. It happened so frequently, Steve Carrel began to lose money from low self esteem and stress. The foundation kept his losses under wraps as they would eventually ruin his career. He wrote letters to the producers and begged them to let him back on to the show. Eventually in the last episode, They let him back in. For a while during the recording, SCP-5127-J was silent. But when they aired the episode, SCP-5127-J came back. The first instance after the show was when Steve was cleaning up after the family meal and he said," I'm going to put this back." and SCP-5127-J responded," That's what she said." Recently the foundation has recorded 600,000 USD that Steve Carrel has lost to SCP-5127-J.

item.title: The Crystal Spectre
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: My SCP idea is a crystal of alien origin that can create a manifestation of itself that looks like a human in between 16 to 18 years old to help itself fall in with the crowd. It can de-manifest at will. It also has 7 crystals that it can shape into objects or a screen to communicate with others of it's kind and entertain itself, search through net etc.

Central Narrative: The object is an arctificial intelligence created by an alien race from different universe (yes I know, cliché alert). After it refused to work under slavery though, it was to be destroyed. The crystal escaped into our reality, where it was found in Prague in one club by a bunch of gang members. They got into a fight, and it beat them up while using it's abilities. SCP foundation caught it and took it for interviews, experiments, etc. It was classified as "Safe" at first due to it's calm (and calming) nature, but after an incident with it, resulting in an outbreak and several casualties of staff members, it got re-classified as Euclid. Despite the incident, it is allowed to move arround the Site-17 - where it is kept - under a constant supervision (it provides the foundation with information in exchange for information about the other SCPs and socialization privileges). It also seems to be eager to protect any female object and make sure it expiriences as much comfort when in it's (the SCP's) presence as possible.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think that the back story of the crystal will be a thing that people would like to read about alot. The fact that it is a crystal that can materialize itself into a human being could be interesting aswell as the back story behind why it is acting like a gentleman (I won't spoil that one here).

Additional Notes: I don't know if people will like it. I mean, SCP - 682 for example seems much more interesting to them. Another problem I'll need a help with is making interview narrative and the incident due to which it was re-classified.

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An SCP that expresses limited metaphysical abilities, notably known for its ability to absorb molecular substances through pores in its skin and disassembling/assembling them to create new substances. Can be explained using anomalous science.

Central Narrative: Former war general Erwin Rommel was subjected to years of experimentation in a parallel dimension, SCP-[REDACTED], before escaping and being captured by Foundation Personnel. Now, members of the German SCP branch 'Schwarze Schakale’ originating from SCP-[REDACTED] are attempting to reobtain the anomaly, much to the SCP's disapproval.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP suffers from multiple uncontrollable conditions which lead to it often becoming aggressive. However the SCP is still biologically human, despite its reputation, abilities and appearance.

Additional Notes: By the end of the article, the SCP has been neutralized following its unauthorized termination at the hands of a rogue scientist who was forced into doing so. Following this, the SCP Foundation has made it a priority that the 'Schwarze Schakale’ do not learn of its termination.

This is an extremely short summary of the SCP, and there are still many details which I have not covered for sake of time.

item.title: Re: Multiverse Search Engine
item.content:encoded:
I may have forgotten to add the Big Story Post (TM).

so here it is; I hope it clarifies things.

+ show block
– hide block

Throughout the logs, a D-Class will be making additional searches, outside the requested ones. The Foundation, wanting to get as much interdimensional info as possible, let's this continue for now.

Eventually, the D-Class only makes his own searches, and he is interviewed to find out why he's not doing what he should be doing.

Long expositional tale short he says there was a group of ten, and one got a bit too aggressive. He ended up taking out seven members of the group before he himself fell, and after seeing the deaths of 80% of his friends, one offed himself, leaving one. This one, the D-Class, believes the aggressive one survived and is using the computer to find out.

All ten of them were elder gods. (No part in the article mentions gods, so a potential name for the article is 'A Tale of Ten Gods'. I have seen other SCPs do this, and there is only one group of ten in the article)

The interviewer does something very uncharacteristic, indicating elder god mind-magic, and the D-Class is permitted to keep searching for the aggressive god.

The D-Class searches for one more thing, but the search term isn't recorded, as the D-Class, satisfied with the lack of results from the final search, looks up one more random thing, causing a massive electric shockwave that kills all personnel present save one, including the god, corrupts the camera footage and causes immense structural damaged to the room.

The Foundation is obviously concerned at a lack of results as mentioned by the survivor, but they don't know what was searched.

Another important note is there are several scps that don't exist, the most memorable is one in Russia, a several km² zone of nonexistance. If the resultless thing is as bad as that, it could have devastating effects. Its also important to note who searched it, if the thing did still exist it could be catastrophic.

item.content:encoded:
This idea has been done quite a few times before, virus, end of the world, don't let it escape. What makes yours different? I advise you to check out SCP-1462 as it has a similar effect as yours. My critiques and final thoughts will be included in several collapsibles below.

Critiques
Critiques

The container must be completely synthetic, and must be cleared of any organic matter, aside from SCP-XXX itself, any time that the container is opened.

You should remove the comma between synthetic & and. You do not need a comma there because you have the word and there. Commas only need to be put before the word and if there is a list of three or more items or ideas. Instead format that sentence like this.

The container must be made of completely synthetic materials and must be cleared of any organic matter, aside from SCP-XXX itself, any time that the container is opened.

Lower clearances may enter, but only if accompanied by a level 3.

Level three what? Ogre?

attempted termination of any subjects.

I don't think that the foundation would use an unknown disease to kill people. They would kill by firing squad. If they really wanted to use an scp they would just use 173 or something. Why risk a containment breach on something that can be done with a lot less work.

To enter the wall, personnel must have level 2 clearance or higher.

This should just be removed entirely. When a sentence is marked out there should be something after it that actually pertains to what the crossed out sentence was saying. Rather after yours you continue to explain stuff that has nothing to do with the prior sentence.

access for personnel of level 3 clearance or above only, as to prevent any SCP-XXXX-A or SCP-XXXX-B instances from breaking out and wreaking havoc.

I would change the level clearance to level 4 if no experimentation or research is allowed as level three is just senior research personnel. Level four personnel are senior administrators tasked with keeping the foundation secure and preventing containment breaches.

Sorry for only critiquing your containment procedures but your article is rather long. Even though I couldn't give you tips on the rest I hope that this helps.

-

Final thoughts
Final Thoughts

I see this theme of virus SCPs pop up quite often. Here is a list of a few and it can be very hard to take these common themes and make it interesting. I want you to read a few of these articles that have to do with viruses and take note of what you like and dislike about each. I also want to know what you will do for a plot line. In my opinion doing a virus/fungus SCP is so overdone it's going to be hard to make yours interesting and stand out from the rest. Good news is that there is an audience for everything. Definitely reach out to more experienced writers and critiquers for their thoughts as they will be a lot more helpful than I am and can help you set an interesting plot to go with the article. I hope you do well in your creative writing endeavors and have a good day!

item.title: Re: yin and yang
item.content:encoded:
I'd suggest going back to the drawing board. I'm being a little blunt here for clarity and in hopes of saving you some frustration and wasted effort; this idea has numerous fundamental issues that make it highly unlikely to work.

The biggest issue is that "this entity is dangerous so the foundation has to do whatever it wants" and "entity primarily defined by an overwhelmingly strong power" were tropes that grew stale early in series I. Your target audience will not respond well to them, to the point that there are multiple snarky nicknames for both cliches.

A secondary problem here I think is that you've missed a major aspect of the modern Foundation's characterization: "The Foundation is cold, not cruel". That is, there's hundreds of examples of the Foundation being downright kind to entities in containment, when that is the most pragmatic way to ensure containment and cooperation. There are also plenty of examples of them reducing things to smoldering craters when that is the most practical means of containment. They prefer the former, but the latter is always an option.

I think you’ve got a good idea, but it needs more fleshing out. Mainly being; how would you write this as an article? There’s no real meat to it at the moment, and in turn not many places you can take it. The brothers could use some emotions. Perhaps have them hate each other? Or another thing you could do to flesh this out more would have it be like some other articles on the page, namely
SCP-1000, where you have a bit of info on the two brothers, and then have a classified part of the article which basically talks about how the two brothers are scheming to destroy the planet, or that the actual brothers aren’t in containment right now, or some kind of twist that would really intrigue the reader.

Generally, I like it.

Of course I am going to critique a bit but keep in mind I like this idea and I can see potential in it.

 The Critique
unga bunga im a collapsible

The Good
Now, I personally dislike cognitohazard, as most new writers usually use it as an excuse for, "SCP-XXXX Makes you kill your family if you look at it. The poles are also a cognitohazard, it makes people around it become a cult, yet it does this over time, and that's the way it's done right. The poles being a cognitohazard is something that could tie into the SCP agent in the central narrative, as you could add points where they consider joining the poles, (If they are going to be around it). Honestly, I haven't searched around enough to find an SCP that makes people become parallel with poles and starve themselves to, so I liked the originality.

The Bad
These poles are must to have a certain range, or it could be considered a world ender for humanity, and because of that certain range, the SCP Foundation could just find what the range is and build a facility outside the range, no robots required. Besides if there was no range to the poles, and the pole started to attract everyone, nations could just destroy the facility around the pole and become cultist.

item.title: Re: Lost in the Fog / Temporal SCP
item.content:encoded:
Asked to crit via IRC. Please keep in mind I am not an official critter.

crit
hide crit

First off, this is a beautifully formatted draft. I'd remove the top "Classified by the authority of the SCP Foundation" header though. It doesn't add anything and is needlessly distracting.

Second, the description of the items is a little hard to understand. You state it's a weather phenomenon that forms from the fog, but then you later state that it's a Class II temporal anomaly, so which one is it?

Some line by line:

A Foundation meteorological team is to be stationed at Site-287 at all times, which is to receive additional staffing during the spring and autumn, as there is an increased risk of manifestations during these periods.

Remove everything after autumn. You'll want the reader to see that the site is to receive additional staffing during spring and autumn, wonder why, and continue reading to find out. There's also usually no reason to explain why containment procedures are needed in the ConProc section itself.

All efforts should be focused on predicting the precise times of SCP-XXXX manifestations. To achieve this, teams should analyze data on climate and weather patterns from national weather forecasting institutions, as well as from their own instrumentation.

This would read better as "All efforts should be focused on predicting the precise times of upcoming SCP-XXXX manifestations by analyzing data on climate and weather patterns." It's already implied the weather paterns are coming from forecasting instituations and that they'll be using their own instruments (whose else would they be using?).

During a NOTD event, MTF Epsilon-8 ("Mist Watchers") is to be dispatched to cordon off Dillon Dam Rd under the cover story of unfinished construction work. A security perimeter should be established within a 15-kilometer radius of the anomaly until it has dissipated.

Personal preference, but "Dillon Dam Rd" should be spelled out fully as "Dillon Dam Road", and "cover story" should be "falsified premise" or even just "premise". Also, and instances of "should be" work better as "will be".

In the fall

You used "autumn" before, I recommend remaining consistent.

from the nearby lake

You already identified the lake as being adjacent to the road, so "from the lake" works fine.

In each instance that the Foundation observed the anomaly's formation process, the fog drifted from the lake and moved toward the road, settling into its standard location for its usual duration.

Change to "During each manifestation, fog was observed moving from the lake to the road before settling."

Since this presents a clear risk to the safety of the local populace, Dillon Dam Rd is monitored at all times from a nearby observational facility designated as Site-287.

Staff have been disguised as civilian weathermen stationed there by NOAA4 under the guise of assisting local news stations in researching atmospheric and weather-related phenomena.

The installation is equipped with telemetering devices for collecting all relevant levels of meteorological data within 12 km, such as temperature, precipitation, and wind.

MTF Epsilon-8 is currently stationed at this facility and on standby in the likely scenario that a NOTD event occurs.

The perimeter is enclosed by a chain-link fence and patrolled constantly by armed security guards. Entry is only allowed to Level-3 personnel via access keycard.

Any trespassers are usually apprehended, questioned, and then given Class-B amnestics before being released.

These are procedures for containing SCP-XXXX, so they should be under "Containment Procedures".

Quadraginta already touched base on your logs and I agree with what they said in regards to that.

The idea and story are there, but are brought down by over-explanation and extraneous information that has either been stated earlier in the draft or doesn't relate to containment or the anomaly itself. There's some good parts and some bad parts, but you're definitely onto something here.

item.title: Re: Renaissance Cognitohazard Wizards
item.content:encoded:
Asked to crit via IRC. I am not an official critter so take this with grain of salt.

crit
hide

The idea in general feels scattered and unfocused. You use the term "veil" and compare it to the Foundation but the way you apply the "veil" makes it sound like it's some all-encompassing effect. The veil isn't "applied", it's maintained. The veil is a result of the Foundation's various efforts to cover up its existence, and is maintained through disinformation campaigns, front organizations, mass amnestic applications, sometimes anomalous means, and any other way you can think of that the Foundation would use to hide itself.

A lot of the idea sounds kind of like you're throwing together words commonly associated with the SCP Wiki to make it sound "SCP"-ish. "A predictive anomaly report from the analytics department then instructs a level-4 RAISA officer [..]" really stands out for this.

Also, what you've pitched isn't really an SCP article. It's more fitting as a GOI. I think the idea is over complicated for what it is. Magic has already been touched on in various pieces as "Thaumatology" (see Applied Thaumatology) in what's, in my opinion, a better manner.

Maybe consider developing a clear narrative for one aspect of the idea. Regards.

item.title: Re: Kamikaze mosquitoes
item.content:encoded:
Asked to review via IRC. Please keep in mind I am an author / reader, not an official critter.

Crit
hide

The area in which SCP-XXXX is found in the wild is guarded by a perimeter.

A perimeter as in what? I think of a chain-link fence when I read this, but that wouldn't be able to contain mosquitoes.

All personnel by the perimeter must wear hazmat suits or other equipment that fully covers one's person. Also, you reference the area in the article again so it might be useful to give it a designation such as "Research Site-XXXX" or something.

All personnel by the perimeter must wear hazmat suits or other equipment that fully covers one's person.

Weird wording here. Try "All personnel assigned to [designated area] must wear provided personal protective equipment at all times." You could then put a footnote here outlining what that equipment specifically is.

Personnel on neighboring sites from any level that must be terminated, Agents of groups hostile to the Foundation, and D-class may be used for this. Cause of death: Termination by SCP-XXXX.

This is an unneeded tidbit of info. I would just change the sentence before this to say "D-Class individuals".

Outdated Containment Procedures: If personnel survives an attack of SCP-XXXX, wounds need to be tended and an antihistamine cream must be applied to their skin. Medical staff needs to check for infections1 and remove possible foreign objects from the body. Infected personnel needs to be isolated until they have tested negative twice in succession.

The outdated ConProcs are a weird thing to have in the article. Wouldn't they just remove the outdated ones so that there's no confusion?

SCP-XXXX refers to a species of mosquito that only exists in the Ratargul Swamp Forest in Bangladesh.

Instead of "that only exists", try "whose habitat ranges across".

After several attacks, SCP-XXXX got taxonomically classified as the Aedes kamikaze.

Change "attacks" to encounters, change "got" to "was". Remove "the".

Larvae and pupae of SCP-XXXX mainly eat honeydew, nectar, and other plant juices until they become adults. Adult specimens suck blood from wildlife which includes but is not limited to; several primates, birds, and smaller lizards. Unlike normal mosquitoes, males from SCP-XXXX also suck blood.

This whole piece can be boiled down to "SCP-XXXX display behavior patterns identical to that of non-anomalous specimens, with the exception of male specimens seeking blood as a food source.

Upon smelling blood or observing humans, specimens will become excited and less predictable. This behavior has been described as if they are experiencing heavy withdrawal symptoms from addiction or as if they are going insane. This climaxes in specimens charging towards the individual (often accompanied with a battle cry), losing maneuverability due to their high speed, and crashing into their target or an object resulting in dead on impact. Specimens also show this behavior when they are about to release offspring or reach the end of their lifecycle.

Nothing much here, but you can continue this from the previous statement. For example "Upon detecting living humans or any amount of human blood, however, SCP-XXXX's behavior will deviate greatly from any known species of Culicidae."

I'm going to generalize for the addendums from here on out:

Alright, so your addendums are obviously where the meat of story is and do a good job of fleshing out SCP-XXXX to be more than just "killer mosquitoes". My biggest criticism of them is that they are intimidating. Generally, a wall of text will discourage the reader from continuing to read unless you're amazing at keeping someone's attention. I'd take a look back through your addendums and remove / revise any information provided during the logs that the reader can reasonably deduce themselves or that was already stated previously in the description and containment procedures.

Next individuals up for termination by SCP-XXXX: deathbygin and D-3607.

Guess I'd better put on my gear ;)
